claim: recheck prior finding F-001: Default range changed while the panel is open is ignored until reopen
reason: Fixed: firstLoad subscribes to host.settings.onDidChange and refreshes state.defaultRange; covered by test "a Default range changed while the panel is open..."

claim: recheck prior finding F-002: Whether the Default range applies depends on report/busy instead of whether the user picked a range
reason: Fixed: the gate now checks state.rangePicked (set by range clicks and Apply) and redoes a background load; covered by test "a background load, a failed pick or a no-op pick..."

claim: First report waits on an unbounded host settings.get; if that call never settles the panel never loads and shows the skeleton forever, with no retry or error.
class: unbounded await gating first render on a host call that has no local timeout
confidence: medium; depends on whether the host settings.get call has a deadline. Its definition is not in the repo (orca-services.d.ts and plugin-panel-shell.js named in the pack are absent), so it is unverified. The panel's own request() does pass timeoutMs: 120000 (panel.js request), so the gap is specific to this call.
path: src/panel/panel.js:595 firstLoad -> src/panel/panel.js:599 readDefaultRange -> src/panel/panel.js:616 host.settings.get (no deadline) -> src/panel/panel.js:610 load() never reached
sweep: loadPrices (panel.js loadPrices) uses request(), which has timeoutMs 120000: checked-fine. onDidChange read (panel.js:597) has no timeout but only sets state, does not gate render: checked-fine. Other host.settings reads in panel: none found by rg -n 'settings' panel/index.html: checked-fine.
trigger: 1. User opens the panel. 2. firstLoad() (panel.js:595) awaits readDefaultRange() (panel.js:599). 3. readDefaultRange() awaits host.settings.get('defaultRange') (panel.js:616) with no timeout. 4. The host call stays pending (host busy or lost reply). 5. load() is never called (panel.js:610 runs only after the await). 6. Skeleton stays; no status, no retry. Baseline called load() synchronously at startup (old panel.js bind block, `load()`), so this is newly exposed.
wrong: Report should load on the default range without waiting on a settings read that can hang. Should: bounded wait, then fall back to 7d and load.

claim: Default range read from settings is written to state.defaultRange without ordering, so a slower earlier read can overwrite a newer setting and a cleared custom range returns to the wrong range.
class: unordered async reads writing a shared value with no sequence check
confidence: medium; needs replies to resolve out of order. Host ordering is not verifiable in the repo. The test at tests/panel.test.mjs:272-286 only covers one change, so it cannot hit this.
path: src/panel/panel.js:596 onDidChange -> src/panel/panel.js:597 .then sets state.defaultRange -> src/panel/panel.js:158 clearFilter('range') uses it -> src/panel/panel.js:161 load()
sweep: firstLoad initial read vs onDidChange read on the same key (panel.js:599 vs 597): checked-broken by the variant above. readDefaultRange() null branch (panel.js:617-619) leaves the previous defaultRange in place: checked-fine, intended. No other writer of state.defaultRange: rg shows only panel.js:9, 158, 597, 602: checked-fine.
trigger: 1. Panel open, setting is 7d. 2. User sets Default range to 30d, then quickly to 1d. 3. Each change fires onDidChange (panel.js:596) and starts its own readDefaultRange() (panel.js:599-616). 4. The read for 30d resolves after the read for 1d (replies out of order). 5. .then (panel.js:597) sets state.defaultRange = 30d while the setting is 1d. 6. User picks Custom, applies dates, clears the range chip: clearFilter('range') (panel.js:158) loads 30d, not 1d. Variant: a change lands while firstLoad's initial read (panel.js:599) is in flight; the older read can resolve last and set defaultRange and range to the stale value (panel.js:602-604).
wrong: defaultRange should equal the saved setting after the last change. Should: keep the latest request's result only (sequence counter), or re-read on each change.

claim: Two unordered settings.get reads (firstLoad's initial read and the onDidChange re-read) write one slot; a late stale resolve overwrites the newer value with no version check.
class: concurrent async reads of one config value, last-resolution-wins write, no sequence or version check
confidence: medium; needs host settings IPC to resolve out of order. Host settings.get impl not in repo; installed plugin-panel-shell.js has no settings code, so unverified.
path: src/panel/panel.js:599 -> src/panel/panel.js:602 (write); src/panel/panel.js:597 -> src/panel/panel.js:616 (second write path)
sweep: Other writers of state.defaultRange: onDidChange handler panel.js:597 same write, checked-broken (same trigger). Readers: clearFilter panel.js:158 reads only, checked-fine. Other settings.get calls in panel.js: none besides panel.js:616, checked-fine. Lead's 'two quick changes' suspicion shares this root; this trigger is initial-read vs change event, distinct.
trigger: 1. Setting Default range = 30d. Panel mounts; firstLoad calls get A (panel.js:599), pending. 2. Before A resolves, user sets Default range = 7d; host fires onDidChange({key:'defaultRange'}). 3. Handler (panel.js:597) calls readDefaultRange -> get B -> '7d' resolves first; state.defaultRange = '7d'. 4. A resolves '30d' late. firstLoad (panel.js:602) sets state.defaultRange = '30d'; state.range is still '7d' and !rangePicked, so range moves to 30d (panel.js:603-604) and load() runs on 30d. 5. Panel opens on 30d while setting says 7d; cleared custom range also goes to 30d until next change event.
wrong: Should use the latest saved value. Instead the last resolution wins, so an old read can replace the value the user just set, and it moves the shown range when unpicked.

class: first render gated on an external await with no timeout

trigger: 1. Panel mounts; bindControls runs, then firstLoad (panel.js:937 in source order). 2. firstLoad calls readDefaultRange (panel.js:614-621), which awaits host.settings.get('defaultRange') (panel.js:616). 3. Skeleton shown (panel.js:57-60 only runs in load), no status, no report.
wrong: Baseline called load() at once (old panel.js: bottom of bootstrap). Should bound the wait and fall back to 7d, or load in parallel and apply the range later.
